fixes.explanation: Right on the money, friend. The song says, "He has founded His city on the holy mountains." Notice who does the founding: He does. The city's foundation is His doing. That's a city built by the best builder there is.

There it is, friend. "Glorious things are ascribed to you, O city of God." The song turns and talks right to the city, like a friend leaning over to say something good about you. Then the verse ends with "Selah."
Not hidden, friend. The song says, "Glorious things are ascribed to you, O city of God." The song talks right to the city, and what it says is glorious. Hidden isn't the word in this verse.

Yes, friend, and this is the big moment of the song. The voice mentions Rahab and Babylon, along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush, and says, "This one was born in Zion." Those are names from outside Israel. I'd love to see the faces in the crowd when they hear it.

That would be a closed door, friend, and this song doesn't close it. The voice says, "This one was born in Zion." It says that when it mentions Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush. Nothing in the verse says to stay outside.

A stranger, friend? Not in this song. When the voice mentions Rahab and Babylon, along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush, it says, "This one was born in Zion." That's the line the voice gives, and stranger isn't in it.

Yes, friend. "The LORD will record in the register of the peoples: 'This one was born in Zion.'" A register is an official list, and the LORD is the one who records in it. Then the verse ends with "Selah," like verse 3 did.

That's the band, friend. The verse says, "Singers and pipers will proclaim…" and then, "All my springs of joy are in You." Voices and pipes, together. I think a song about a city this glad should end with music.
Close on the music part, friend, but not on the players. The verse says, "Singers and pipers will proclaim…" Priests and trumpeters aren't the ones named there. Imagine the pipes instead.

A fancy lineup, friend, but they're not in this verse. It says, "Singers and pipers will proclaim…" and then, "All my springs of joy are in You." The ones making music are singers and pipers. I'd still buy a ticket.
